To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the protein–protein interactions that are involved in cell signaling are highly dynamic; (2) the dynamics of these interactions are modulated by the presence and binding of ligands; and (3) the dynamics of the interactions are important in determining the biological function of the proteins.
the protein–nucleotide interactions in the ribosome are similar to the interactions observed in the ribosome and that the interactions are conserved between the two ribosomes.

the protein–protein interfaces are more hydrophobic, more polar, more charged, and more acidic than previously thought; and that the protein–DNA interfaces have a different character from the protein–protein ones.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of proteins and their interactions with other molecules, and the information that is contained in these structures.
the structural basis for protein–protein interactions and protein–DNA recognition.
the development of new methods and algorithms for the analysis, prediction and modeling of protein structures and their interactions.
